TEXT.English: [H1]Pimedasus Helendav[\H1] [BOLD]Last Princess of the Dread Host[\BOLD] [BOLD]Lived: [\BOLD] The Reunion of the Princesses, Year 1 - ???? [PARAGRAPH:2][BOLD]Background:[\BOLD] [TAB]In another age and another reality, Pimedasus' life would have been remembered as one of friendship, discovery, and harmony. She would have stood beside five wonderful friends, defeated ancient evils, and helped guide Equestria into a new era. This world, however, was not that Equestria, and Pimedasus Helendav's life on Equus was far more different than the light and harmony of her forebears and the alternative realities of innumerable decisions which had shaped them. [PARAGRAPH:1]Pimedasus' story began as the story of Twilight Sparkle. Her world was, at first, remarkably similar to the peaceful Equestria known from the Prime timeline. Twilight was a librarian in Ponyville, a devoted student of Princess Celestia, and the bearer of the Element of Magic. She had met her first forever friends, kept a comfortable home, and imagined many a future which, if all went well, seemed destined to unfold according to the ancient prophecies of Equestrian history. But the prophecies were wrong. When Twilight and Celestia investigated the ancient legend surrounding the return of Nightmare Moon, they discovered that the coming darkness would not be a single catastrophe. Instead, an entire coalition of enemies had been assembled against the great pony nation of Equestria. King Sombra, Nightmare Moon, Queen Chrysalis, Cozy Glow, Grogar the Father of Monsters reborn, and an unreformed Starlight Glimmer became the principal forces of the enemy alliance. This coalition of darkness had formed beneath the influence of Discord, whose hatred of his ancient imprisonment had never faded. [PARAGRAPH:1]Princess Celestia, realizing that Equestria faced an enemy unlike anything it had ever encountered, accelerated her newest student's education in every discipline she believed the future ruler of Equestria might require. The young librarian became a military commander, war mage, diplomat, researcher, and student of statecraft. Twilight Sparkle became Equestria's greatest weapon, the Princess' most wonderful success, professed by many a pony to lead the battered civilization into a glorious future of harmony and peace unlike any ever seen before. With her spellbooks, enchanted armor, and the Elements of Harmony beside her, Twilight defeated enemies that had threatened her world for generations. Grogar fell. Discord was banished. Chrysalis, Cozy Glow, and Starlight were defeated. By every conventional measure, Equestria had won the Great Long War - yet victory came at a terrible price. [PARAGRAPH:1]The final catastrophe came not from an enemy army, but from within the royal family itself. Princess Celestia attempted to restore her sister Luna through the Elements of Harmony. The Lunar Princess, however, had endured a thousand years of isolation upon the Moon before her prophesied return. Whatever remained of Luna after that imprisonment could no longer be reached. Whether it was Discord's final curse, a talon's snap only briefly spotted by Twilight Sparkle, or a terrible twist of fate played upon the first family of Equestria was never known before the end. Celestia was forced to seal her sister away once more, this time without the hope that she would ever be restored; the act destroying the soft heart still beating inside the Solar Princess. Already exhausted by the Great Long War and burdened by the destruction surrounding her, Celestia transformed into her own nightmare: Daybreaker. [PARAGRAPH:1]Twilight had spent years preparing for the possibility that Equestria might someday face another great enemy. She had never prepared to fight her mentor. The final battle of the war was fought between Twilight Sparkle and her dear Princess who had once took her under wing and taught Twilight all that she knew so that she may one day lead Equestria into the Golden Age to end all Golden Ages. Twilight won. Of course she won. She had always won, like she did ever since she had stepped through the doors of Celestia's school and performed the wonderous feats of magic recorded in the private annuls of Celestia's journals. Nor would she would ever stop winning or give up the eternal fight. She had been trained, guided, and mentored to do just that. And yet... there was no celebration, no cheering crowd, for there was no Equestria left to save. [PARAGRAPH:1]When Twilight finally emerged from the battlefield, she discovered that the land she had fought to protect had become a wasteland of heat, ash, blackened earth, and magical ruin. The catastrophe had consumed the population of Equestria. Twilight's salvation came from an unlikely source. While studying the magical devastation left behind by the war, she discovered ancient parchment colllections whose contents seemed impossible to have existed within her world. The Histories of Civilization, by an author referred to as "Solais a Tuath", which proclaimed itself as one of a mystical series of volumes that, despite their age, appeared unblemished and rather readable well into the modern times. The strangest thing about them was their source: The publisher mentioned was "Equestrian Crown Productions", yet Celestia had never mentioned owning them, no surviving library's record ever laid claim to saving them for public reading. Furthermore, no extant civilization of the continents of Equus ever knew about them before Pimedasus laid eyes upon, despite her searches. [PARAGRAPH:1]Within their pages were records of magic, civilizations, history, warfare, and phenomena that extended far beyond the limits of her own reality. Through these texts she learned to reverse the damage done to the land, restoring Equestria's physical form. Twilight, nevertheless, had nothing left to lose and everything to gain, so she continued forwards with all her desperate, wonderous hope. But she could not restore what had truly been lost: The soul of Equestria. Twilight Sparkle eventually came to accept a terrible truth: she could heal the world, but she could not bring back the moment before everything fell apart. Yet. And so she abandoned the name Twilight Sparkle. She became Pimedasus Helendav, the Glowing Darkness. The Last Princess of Equestria. Pimedasus devoted herself to the study of even the most forbidden and esoteric magic, searching the boundaries between life and death for a path back to the world she remembered. She sought not conquest, nor immortality, nor domination. She sought a way to undo the single chain of events that had destroyed everything she loved. Among the greatest secrets she uncovered were the ancient arts of reconstruction and necromantic preservation. With these powers, Pimedasus accomplished a miracle that was also a tragedy. She recreated Equestria. [PARAGRAPH:1]Every citizen returned. Every ordinary pony whose life had once filled the kingdom with warmth and life, carrying their memories, personalities, ambitions, talents, and appearances exactly as they had been. The new Equestria under Pimedasus Helendav was not an army of mindless undead. Its citizens laughed, worked, dreamed, and remembered. They were themselves in every way that could be measured. Beneath it all, however, behind the lights of Fluttershy's eyes, behind everypony's eyes, there was an absence that no living pony could ever truly reconcile. And Pimedasus knew this fact, and yet she loved her ponies still anyway. A beautiful imitation of a lost song. The Soul of Ponydom, played through the instruments of the world once more.Other civilizations eventually gave Pimedasus' nation a name, calling it the Dread Host. From a distance, the Dread Host could be almost indistinguishable from the Equestria that had existed before the war. Its towns functioned. Its citizens worked. Its schools taught. Its farms produced food. Its princess ruled from Canterlot. And yet beneath the illusion was something profoundly unnatural. The Dread Host maintained no true cycle of life and death, for its citizens, Pimedasus Helendav included, discovered that they could not age as the years passed by. Unlike Twilight herself, whose immortality was unexplainable, the ponies of the Dread Host were just happy to remain beside their friends, their family, their light once more. The achievement she had enshrined through this act of recreation was simultaneously Pimedasus' greatest triumph and perhaps her greatest failure. Pinkie Pie, the Element of Laughter. Fluttershy, the Element of Kindness. Rarity, the Element of Generosity. Applejack, the Element of Honesty, and Rainbow Dash, the Element of Loyaity. More remarkably still, the Elements of Harmony continued to recognize them as their bearers. Pimedasus had therefore recreated not merely five ponies who had once warriors for harmony and light, but the five ponies who had once been the most important people in her life. Pimedasus Helendav eventually discovered a portal within her nation's borders, a swirling, impossible passage connecting her world to the countless realities of Equus maintained by Yggdrasil. She stepped through, allowing the Dread Host to follow her into the wider multiverse. Now, the Glowing Darkness travels between civilizations seeking the ultimate prize: the secrets of time itself. Her goal is not simply to travel backward. She wants to find a way to return to the moment before everything went wrong. Before the Great Long War, before Celestia became Daybreaker, before the death of Equestria, before she became Pimedasus Helendav. She wants to become Twilight Sparkle again, to see her five friends alive in the way they were meant to be alive. She wants Celestia to remain Celestia, and for Luna to finally come home. She wants Ponyville to be a place where the greatest problem of the day might once again be a friendship lesson. She wants the original Equestria - bBut there is a terrible complication. Pimedasus' Equestria is no longer simply a lost world. It is inhabited. Her resurrected ponies have lives. The other civilizations with which she had fleeting, harried contact have histories of their own. They have memories, relationships, ambitions. Indeed, Pimedasus cannot simply erase the Dread Host in order to restore the world that existed before it. Thus her search for time magic is also a search for an answer to an impossible moral problem: Can she restore the life she lost without destroying the lives she created? For now, she continues to search. The Dread Host travels with her. And wherever Pimedasus Helendav walks, five familiar ponies walk beside her once more. Not alive, but neither truly dead. Together, just as they are always meant to be. For Pimedasus, that is enough to keep walking. For now.
